fields.options:
Add this to your Print Format's HTML. Leave Anchor Text above at its default - the same value works for every template regardless of size, since size lives entirely in the HTML, not here:

<div>For, Company Name</div>
<br><br>
##DIGITAL_SIGN_ANCHOR:160x60##
<br><br>
<div>Authorised Signatory</div>

The stamp centres on the anchor and expands equally up and down from it - so put roughly equal <br> tags both above and below the anchor, not all on one side. Plain <br> line breaks reserve space far more reliably than a div with a declared height (some PDF engines don't respect an explicit height reliably) - each <br> is roughly one line's worth of space at your font size. Add or remove them to adjust the gap.

The :WxH height is an upper bound, not a forced size - the stamp draws tight to however many lines are actually enabled below (Stamp Font Size / Stamp Line Spacing in Digital Sign Settings control exactly how big each line renders). It only uses the full declared height if the content genuinely can't fit any shorter.

The :WxH suffix is optional and detected automatically from what's actually rendered - add it in the Print Format's HTML to size that particular template; leaving it off (plain ##DIGITAL_SIGN_ANCHOR##) falls back to 160x80.

Keep the width matching the number in the anchor text - width is used as-is for the stamp's actual drawn width; height is just the ceiling.

Use color:#ffffff (matching the background), not opacity:0 - some PDF engines skip painting opacity:0 text entirely, dropping it from the searchable text layer too. If the surrounding background isn't white, match this color to it instead.
